title: Round Table Foundation funded by Army, Navy and CIA

tellings.quote: they were just like flocking to this place, basically giving him money to do research. And this was, yeah, '49, '50, very early.

plain: Around 1949 and 1950, a small research group in Rockland, Maine, called the Round Table Foundation is said to have drawn money from the US Army, the Navy and the CIA, the country's foreign intelligence agency, all flocking to fund the man running it. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this, pointing to letters from those agencies to the foundation, and it would mean the military and spies were backing its unusual research very early on.
